text:
kim_support: FYI customer reported a big p99 jump around 2026-03-12 14:12 UTC and some 502s. They say our dashboard shows p99 at ~1.2s but traces show many tails at 3-6s. Request example: request_id=req_0a12b3. Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/latency_prod?orgId=1

jake_oncall: Thanks Kim. Can you paste the exact panel/query you're looking at and the timeframe? Is this isolated to the inference endpoint or auth/proxy?

kim_support: Panel is "api.request_latency.p99 (last 1h)" on service=llm-inference, env=prod. Customer observed it during a high-volume ingest at ~14:10. They also saw a handful of 502s with the same request_id prefix.

priya_sre: Quick hypothesis: metrics aggregation mismatch. Our dashboard panel uses the "percentile" function over rollup buckets (from the rollup service) while the raw trace quantile from the tracing UI is per-request aggregated. That can under/overestimate tails depending on windowing. Also need to check proxy retry inflation — if proxy retries count as new requests in prometheus, p99 can look worse.

leo_platform: Confirming: the rollup pipeline emits exponential histogram summaries to the metrics store with bucket boundaries at [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1,2,5]. The dashboard panel was accidentally switched to the "apply_avg" quantile aggregator last week during a panel edit (cc @dash-team). That explains the ~1.2s number vs trace.

metrics-bot: alert: p99_spike_detected service=llm-inference window=5m start=2026-03-12T14:09:00Z end=2026-03-12T14:14:00Z peak_p99=3.8s rule_id=latency-tail-5m

jake_oncall: Good catch Leo. Two follow-ups: (1) Are proxy retries / 502s being deduped in the rollup? (2) Any auth spikes or token refresh storms around 14:10?

priya_sre: I pulled logs for req_0a12b3: I see upstream latency at the model pool (GPU queueing) and ~3 retry attempts at the proxy for some of those requests. The proxy increments a retry counter and re-emits the request metric (we've had this issue before). So prometheus sees 4 attempts for 1 logical request in the worst cases.

kim_support: Customer says they saw a change after we rolled a routing tweak yesterday. Could be related to autoscaler breathing + heavier batching leading to queueing. They need a mitigation ASAP.

leo_platform: Mitigations we can do fast: (A) flip dashboard panel to use raw histogram percentiles (raw_quantile) so customer sees the real trace-aligned number, (B) exclude retry attempts from rollups (short term: drop metric label retry=true in rollup query), (C) temporarily increase pool capacity / reduce max_batch_size for that model to lower queueing. I can push A and B in 20m. C needs a short deploy.

jake_oncall: For the customer reply: give these steps and offer a short-term config to route them to a less-batched model. Also ask them to reproduce with the same request_id so we can correlate logs.

priya_sre: Repro steps I ran: curl -H "X-Request-Id: req_0a12b3" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"<large-batch>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
I saw the same 3-5s tails when payloads hit >10 inputs per request. With batching capped at 4, p99 back to ~600ms.

kim_support: I'll send customer the mitigations and ask them to test reduced batch size. Also will mention we'll fix the dashboard to avoid confusion.

leo_platform: I'll apply the dashboard panel change now and add a short note in the panel description about rollup vs raw. Also adding a temporary rollup filter: `where retry!=true` to the rollup query.

metrics-bot: action_log: panel_update applied by leo_platform at 2026-03-12T14:40:21Z; rollup_query_patch staged in canary

jake_oncall: Priya, can you schedule a follow-up to verify autoscaler behaviour during the peak and whether we should tweak scale thresholds?

priya_sre: On it. I'll run a replay on the load simulator for the model pool and log scaling events. Tentative owner: priya_sre. ETA 3 hours.

kim_support: customer update queued. I'll share the steps and ask for a repro during their next window. Will update thread when they confirm. :thumbsup:
